lines.text: What should I do... People really worked hard for this...
Well... I just found out that I left three key research data files behind...
Really? Thank you so much...! The three data files have been stored in handyterms. Just look for those!
Before I forget, my name's ⟦key|Kitt⟧. I'll stay on the comms and try to tell you what I know about this area.

options: You look terrible. Having a problem?
This place isn't safe. I'll retrieve it for you.
Okay. Leave it to me.

r: You look terrible. Having a problem?
This place isn't safe. I'll retrieve it for you.
Okay. Leave it to me.

lines.text: Thanks for agreeing to help, Endmin...
Those research data files are really important! Please help me retrieve them!
This machine is huge...
Are you talking about the unit at the corridor bend? That's our sample radiation intensity scanner.
I often see Yvonne working that machine on her own. Thought she was using it to run some scans. Turns out she was installing defensive lasers all over the place!
Well, Yvonne does act in mysterious ways...
They're growing so many Originium clusters here...

I adopted a new crystal cultivation approach and tweaked the environmental parameters. I even submitted a paper based on this special cultivation process ... but it's still being peer reviewed by the journal.
Hah! That's the fruit of our project! I actually cultivated the biggest cluster, you know.

scenes.summary: You run into UWST scientist Harper who has not evacced the place. He informs you that no one, including you, is authorized to move research data out of the place.

lines.text: Who ... who the hell are you...?
End... Endministrator...? Oh thank Talos! Someone actually came to this place. I'm ⟦key|Harper⟧, a UWST scientist.
My research... A lifetime of blood and sweat... They're all here. I can't leave them unattended.
I'm ready to die for them! If the LBs come here, they'll have to reckon with me!
Really? Does that mean that I can get ... started on my research again?
Ugh. Fine.
Retrieve a data file? Who asked you to do that?
Got it. But you can't retrieve the files from my place.
This research file is quite special. It cannot be removed from this place. It is furnished with special security and encryption measures.
The file will automatically destroy itself when removed from the terminal.
Well, thanks for swinging by. Try looking elsewhere. Maybe you'll come across the data file you need.

options: Have no fear. I'm the Endministrator of Endfield Industries.
Why didn't you evac?
Someone asked me to retrieve a data file.
Don't worry. There are hardly any LBs nearby.
No. The crisis is still ongoing.
A scientist named Kitt.
A crew mate like you, who stayed despite the dangers.
Got it. I'll think of something else.

lines.text: The abandoned data we found seems to be related to this research project.

scenes.summary: You find Harper again and tell him that you found out the truth from his work diary. The scientist finally decides to give you the data.

lines.text: Endmin, why did you come back?
What do you mean? I don't understand.
Ah ... So you ... found out about it...
I'm so close... SO CLOSE! SO FRIGGIN' CLOSE to success!
I cannot give up! I've committed my entire career and reputation on this thing!
Please, Endmin... Will you ... keep it a secret for me?
Oh, thank you so much... I promise! I'm really *THAT* close!
I won't waste the second chance you gave me, Endmin! I swear!
Ugh. Fine. All the data files are here...
There it goes... Years of my blood, sweat, and tears...
I hope so. I hope they don't shelve this project.
Alright. Let me take a look...
This prototype... It's really different from what I have in mind! Wha ... Why didn't I think of this?
This prototype just gave me a jolt of inspiration! I can totally take another shot at this! Endmin! Can you ... give this to me? I really need it for reference!
Scrap data...? The project owners probably ended up like me. The bottleneck probably trapped them for too long...
I'll also give a copy of my research. Someone must bring a complete backup safely out of this place.

options: You have not been straight with me, Mr. Harper.
I saw your work diary. You are troubled by your research.
I understand. Your secret is safe with me.
Sorry, but I must leave with this data file.
I found some data related to your research. Wanna look?
It's alright. Your efforts will pay off.
Sure. Someone told me it's scrap data. I'll scan you a copy.
